summary:
Two pointers from both ends: each skips characters that aren't letters or digits, then the two characters are
compared case-insensitively. A mismatch means no; meeting in the middle means yes. O(n), no extra memory.

question.md:
Ignoring everything except letters and digits, and ignoring case, does `text` read the same both ways?

- **No letters or digits at all** counts as a mirror.
- **Up to 2 × 10⁵ characters.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Text with no letters or digits at all (`"!? ."`) counts as a mirror.
- Digits count: `"1a1"` is a mirror, `"12"` is not.
- Case is ignored: `A` matches `a`.

think.md:
**Checking a palindrome from both ends.** Put `i` at the start and `j` at the end. If `s[i] ≠ s[j]`, it isn't a
palindrome. If they match, that pair is settled forever, so move both inward. When the pointers meet or cross, every
mirrored pair has matched. That's `n/2` comparisons and no extra memory, and it's the base of every problem in this
pattern.

**Skipping instead of cleaning.** Only letters and digits matter. Rather than building a cleaned copy, let each
pointer step over characters that don't count. Trace on `"Step on no pets!"`:

head: i
j
s[i]
s[j]
action
rows: skip right (not a letter or digit)
skip left (not a letter or digit)
skip right (not a letter or digit)

think.md: The pointers met with no mismatch: **true**.

idea.md: Build the cleaned string (letters and digits, lowercased) and compare it with its reverse. Simple and clearly correct.

lines.text: Keep only letters and digits, lowercased: the text the question actually compares.
A palindrome equals its reverse. C compares the cleaned buffer's two ends instead of building a reversed copy.

walk.title: Keep only letters and digits, lowercase them, and compare the result with its reverse.

limits.md: The copy isn't needed: pointers can skip ignored characters as they go, using O(1) memory.

approaches.title: Two pointers that skip

idea.md:
Two pointers. Each loop step does exactly one thing: skip an ignored character on the left, or on the
right, or compare two counted characters case-insensitively and move both inward.

**Why one action per step.** After a skip, the other side might also need skipping, and the loop handles
that naturally. A pointer never skips a counted character, so every mirrored pair of counted characters
is compared exactly once.

build: Skip ignored characters one side at a time.

lines.text: Pointers at the two ends of the text.
Continue while there are at least two characters between them.
A character that isn't a letter or digit doesn't take part; step past it on that side only.
Two counted characters must match ignoring case; then both pointers move inward.
Every pair matched, including the case with nothing to compare.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** each step moves a pointer. **Space O(1).**

steps.text: The pointers met without a mismatch: true.

walk.title: Two pointers from the ends skip anything that isn't a letter or digit, and compare letters ignoring case.

takeaways.md:
- **Filtered palindrome checks: two pointers that skip.**
- Normalise (case) at comparison time instead of copying.
- **Pitfall:** skipping on both sides in one step and jumping past a character that should be compared.
